references.text: The angel of the Lord appears to people in distress. Here, the angel of the Lord appears to Hagar in the wilderness and strengthens her, just as the angel appeared to Jesus in Gethsemane to strengthen him ([ref:Gen 16:7|Genesis 16:7]).

Jacob wrestled with God through the night in an intense spiritual struggle, which recalls Jesus' struggle in Gethsemane where an angel was sent to strengthen him ([ref:Gen 32:24-30|Genesis 32:24-30]).

An angel came to the prophet Elijah when he was exhausted and discouraged in the wilderness, strengthening him with food and drink. Similarly, an angel was sent from heaven to strengthen Jesus during his suffering ([ref:1 Kgs 19:5-8|1 Kings 19:5-8]).

The psalm promises that God will send his angels to protect the righteous. In Gethsemane this promise is fulfilled when an angel from heaven appears to Jesus and strengthens him ([ref:Ps 91:11-12|Psalms 91:11-12]).
The angels are the Lord's servants who carry out his will. The angel in Gethsemane carries out God's will by strengthening Jesus during his suffering ([ref:Ps 103:20-21|Psalms 103:20-21]).

God promises to strengthen and help his servant. The sending of an angel to strengthen Jesus is a concrete fulfillment of this promise of divine strength in times of trouble ([ref:Isa 41:10|Isaiah 41:10]).

A figure with a human appearance touched Daniel and strengthened him when he was without strength. This is a clear parallel to the angel who strengthened Jesus in Gethsemane ([ref:Dan 10:18-19|Daniel 10:18-19]).
After Jesus' temptation in the wilderness, angels came and served him. In a similar way, Jesus was attended by an angel during his struggle in Gethsemane ([ref:Matt 4:11|Matthew 4:11]).

Matthew's account of Jesus' prayer struggle in Gethsemane provides the context for the angel's coming – Jesus prayed earnestly to his Father that the cup of suffering might be taken from him ([ref:Matt 26:36-39|Matthew 26:36-39]).

The angels are ministering spirits sent out to serve those who will inherit salvation. The angel who strengthened Jesus in Gethsemane is an example of this serving function ([ref:Heb 1:14|Hebrews 1:14]).

The letter to the Hebrews describes Jesus' intense prayer "with loud cries and tears" to him who could save him from death, which corresponds with the Gethsemane scene where the angel strengthened him ([ref:Heb 5:7|Hebrews 5:7]).
